Risk Scoring and the Maintenance Strategy It Drives

Unit 3: Risk, Recalls, and Data Security. Lesson 14 of 60 in CHTM Academy.

A surveyor points at a row of identical infusion pumps and asks why they are inspected annually when the manufacturer's manual says every six months. There is exactly one acceptable answer, and it is not "that is what we have always done". It is a documented, risk-based decision made by qualified people, with the evidence behind it in a file you can produce.

Risk-based inclusion, then risk-based strategy

Two decisions, in order. First, inclusion: does this device belong in the equipment management program at all, and at what level of tracking. Second, strategy: what work does it get, and how often. Both decisions are made from the same inputs.

Scoring input              What it asks
Equipment function         what the device does: life support, therapeutic,
                           diagnostic, analytical, or support. Life support
                           scores highest
Physical risk of failure   the harm a failure could cause: death, injury, a
                           wrong diagnosis, or an inconvenience
Likelihood of failure      how often this model actually fails, from your own
                           history or credible outside data
Maintenance requirement    how much scheduled work it truly needs: filters,
                           batteries, calibration, moving parts, or almost none
Incident history           the number, frequency, and nature of past failures
                           and service requests on identical or very similar
                           equipment
Backup availability        whether an alternative or backup device is available
                           in time if this one fails

Scoring models and their thresholds

A scoring model turns those inputs into one number, usually by scoring each input on a short scale and combining them with a published formula. The bands that separate high, medium, and low are set by the hospital in its own written methodology; there is no national threshold to look up, and a manager who quotes one is quoting nothing. What matters for the exam and for a surveyor is that the scale, the formula, and the bands are written down before the scoring starts, applied the same way to every device type, and approved by whoever owns the equipment management plan.

Worked, on this course's own model: all six inputs, each scored 1 to 5, added into one number. The deep dive scores more devices on exactly this model and the same bands.

Device           Func  Phys  Like  Maint  Inc  Back  Score  Band
Ventilator         5     5     3     5      3    5      26  high
Infusion pump      4     4     3     3      3    1      18  high
Diagnostic ECG     3     3     2     3      1    1      13  medium
Exam light         1     1     3     1      1    1       8  low
Bands in this example: 18 and above high, 11 to 17 medium, 10 and below low

What each band gets

  • High: full scheduled maintenance at the manufacturer's interval, with preventive maintenance, safety testing, and performance verification all delivered, on the critical equipment list, and a backup plan for failure.
  • Medium: scheduled maintenance at an interval the risk assessment supports, which may be longer than the manufacturer's, with the evidence on file.
  • Low: inspection only, or in the right circumstances run to failure, also called breakdown or reactive maintenance, where the device is inexpensive, failure harms nobody, and a replacement is on the shelf.

Any change away from the manufacturer's recommendations lives inside a documented AEM program, decided by qualified personnel on a risk assessment. Three things may never go into one: imaging and radiologic equipment, whether diagnostic or therapeutic; medical laser devices; and new equipment with too little maintenance history to support a risk-based decision. New equipment is maintained to the manufacturer's recommendations until that history exists. Equipment in the program must be readily identifiable as such, and so must critical equipment, because that is exactly where a surveyor looks first.

Documenting the rationale, and reviewing it

The file per equipment type holds the inputs with their values, the formula, the band, the activities and frequencies chosen, the qualified person who decided, and the date. Then it gets reviewed, because a score made on a thin history is a hypothesis. Re-score when the failure history changes, when an incident happens on that model, when the manufacturer issues a notice or changes its guidance, when the fleet grows or shrinks, and at the interval the plan sets. And once you have set an interval, you must follow it strictly; an alternative program is a different schedule, never permission to improvise.

Exam tip: the risk inputs are equipment function, physical risk of failure, likelihood of failure, maintenance requirement, incident history, and backup availability. The hospital writes its own thresholds. Imaging and radiologic equipment, lasers, and new equipment without history cannot go into an alternative program, and whatever frequency you set, you must then follow.
Remember
Equipment function, physical risk, likelihood of failure, maintenance requirement, incident history, and backup availability combine into one score whose band decides full scheduled maintenance, a longer interval, inspection only, or run to failure, all documented before the fact.
Deeper explanation

Risk Scoring and the Maintenance Strategy It Drives, explained slowly

Building a scoring model you can defend

There is no national threshold to look up, so the hospital writes its own and writes it down first. Here is one complete methodology, with this course's own 1 to 5 scales.

Equipment function           Physical risk of failure
5  life support              5  death
4  therapeutic               4  injury
3  diagnostic                3  misdiagnosis or mistreatment
2  analytical                2  delay in care
1  support or utility        1  inconvenience only

Likelihood of failure        Maintenance requirement
5  fails more than once a    5  extensive: calibration, filters, batteries,
   year per unit                moving parts
4  roughly annually          4  significant scheduled work
3  every two to three years  3  moderate
2  rarely                    2  minor
1  almost never              1  essentially none

Incident history             Backup availability
5  documented events on      5  no alternative device anywhere
   this or very similar      3  an alternative exists on another unit
   equipment                 1  identical spares on the shelf
3  service requests but no
   patient events
1  none

The worksheet, scored and banded

Device type        Func Phys Like Maint Inc Back  Score  Band   Strategy
Ventilator           5    5    3     5    3    5     26  high   manufacturer
                                                                 interval, full
                                                                 scheduled
                                                                 maintenance,
                                                                 critical list
Infusion pump        4    4    3     3    3    1     18  high   manufacturer
                                                                 interval; spares
                                                                 on the shelf
Anesthesia machine   5    5    2     5    1    3     21  high   manufacturer
                                                                 interval
Diagnostic ECG       3    3    2     3    1    1     13  med    annual, risk
                                                                 assessment on
                                                                 file
Infant scale         2    1    2     2    1    1      9  low    annual
                                                                 inspection and
                                                                 verification only
Exam light           1    1    3     1    1    1      8  low    run to failure,
                                                                 documented
Bands: 18 and above high, 11 to 17 medium, 10 and below low

This is the same model and the same bands the lesson works, extended to six device types. The bands are this methodology's own, published before the scoring and applied to every device type the same way. That is the defensible part. A surveyor is not checking your arithmetic against a national table; there is no national table. A surveyor is checking that a written method, approved by whoever owns the equipment management plan, was applied by qualified people and then followed.

What the alternative program may and may not hold

Question                          Answer
What may be changed               how often maintenance, inspection, and
                                  testing happen, and what they include
On what authority                 a risk assessment by qualified personnel,
                                  hospital employees or contractors
What may NEVER be included        imaging and radiologic equipment, diagnostic
                                  or therapeutic; medical laser devices; new
                                  equipment without enough maintenance history
What blocks a change anyway       any other federal or state law, or a
                                  condition of participation, that requires the
                                  manufacturer's schedule
New equipment                     manufacturer's recommendations until there is
                                  enough history from the hospital, its
                                  contractor, or nationally recognized sources
Evidence required per type        function and consequences of failure, how
                                  serious the likely harm is, likelihood of
                                  failure, maintenance requirements,
                                  availability of alternative or backup
                                  devices, incident history of identical or
                                  very similar equipment
Documentation                     written policies and procedures, the risk
                                  methodology, the evidence per type, and the
                                  activities and frequencies chosen
Adherence                         follow the activities and frequencies you
                                  set, strictly
Identification                    equipment in the program must be readily
                                  identifiable, and so must critical equipment

Re-scoring: the triggers and what changed

Trigger                              Example outcome
A patient event on this model        incident history rises from 1 to 5; the
                                     band moves from medium to high and the
                                     interval returns to the manufacturer's
A year of clean history on a         likelihood falls; the medium band is
device with a thin record            confirmed rather than assumed
The manufacturer changes its         the baseline changed; re-assess the
guidance or issues a notice          whole type
The fleet drops from 20 units to 3   backup availability rises from 1 to 5
A new service is added that makes    function and physical risk both rise
the device the only one of its kind
The review interval in the plan      scheduled re-score, whether or not
arrives                              anything changed

What to memorize

Inputs            equipment function, physical risk of failure, likelihood of
                  failure, maintenance requirement, incident history, backup
                  availability
Thresholds        set by the hospital, written before the scoring, applied
                  uniformly, approved
High              manufacturer interval, full scheduled maintenance, critical
                  equipment list
Medium            an interval the risk assessment supports, evidence on file
Low               inspection only, or documented run to failure
Never in an AEM   imaging and radiologic, lasers, new equipment without
program           history
Then              follow the frequency you set, strictly
